channel.title: Market Pressure Map · Indian markets
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Indian market sectors and the rupee, bonds, inflation and foreign flows.

item.title: Wholesale inflation rises to a series-high 12.29% in October as fuel and power inflation hits 32.84%
item.description:
Up from 11.39% in September but just below the roughly 12.4% expected. Manufactured-goods inflation eased to 9.54% from 9.76% and food to 8.58% from 8.66%. Economists see October as the likely peak. Escalating for a third month.

Why it matters: Double-digit wholesale inflation squeezes manufacturers' margins and feeds into retail prices already above the RBI's ceiling, though easing core components and softer crude hint at a peak.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −2, Bond market (G-Secs) −1, Growth outlook −1

Confidence: high · horizon: months

item.title: Sensex gains 510 points to 82,102.85 and Nifty 0.58% to 25,291.10 as FMCG and banks lead
item.description:
Autos, realty and pharma lagged and broader indices stayed under pressure on Monday. On Tuesday the Sensex opened about 46 points higher at 82,150.62 despite a 2.5% Nasdaq fall. Reverses Friday's decline.

Why it matters: Foreign buying and cheaper crude are outweighing record wholesale inflation; India is being treated as a refuge from the global AI-stock sell-off.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +2

Confidence: high · horizon: days

item.title: Foreign investors buy a net ₹4,865 crore on Monday, an eleventh straight session of buying
item.description:
Domestic institutions sold about ₹3,519 crore, per provisional data. November's foreign buying of about $8.9 billion is the highest monthly total on record. Ongoing.

Why it matters: Persistent inflows support equities and the rupee even as US yields and the dollar stay high; domestic funds are supplying the shares.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows +2, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1, Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Rupee reported 27 paise higher at 93.92 per dollar on inflows and softer crude; reports differ on the close
item.description:
Agency reports put the provisional close at 93.92 from Friday's weaker level, though one outlet said it stayed below 94. The dollar index rose to about 103.6. Reversing two days of losses.

Why it matters: Foreign equity inflows and a 3.6% fall in crude offset a strong dollar; analysts still warn of pressure from Gulf tensions and inflation.

Market gauges: Rupee +1

Confidence: low · horizon: days

item.title: 10-year G-Sec yield edges up to 7.31% after the wholesale inflation print
item.description:
The benchmark closed at 7.31%, marginally higher than Friday's 7.30%. States are due to sell ₹23,300 crore of bonds on Tuesday. Ongoing: up from 7.19% ten days ago.

Why it matters: High inflation prints and steady supply keep yields elevated, raising borrowing costs and limiting bank treasury gains despite foreign debt inflows.

Market gauges: Bond market (G-Secs) −1, Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Unemployment rate falls to 4.9% in October, the lowest in about eight months
item.description:
Down from 5.0% in September and 5.2% a year earlier. Urban unemployment eased to 6.7% from 6.9%, rural held at 4.2%, and female participation rose to 35%. Improving, though partly seasonal farm work.

Why it matters: A firmer labour market supports household income and consumption even as inflation erodes purchasing power.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: months

item.title: Brent falls 3.6% to settle at $92.44 as Gulf exports recover and the IEA sees a 1.7 million bpd surplus
item.description:
WTI settled 3.2% lower at $85.72. Prices fell despite a second Iranian attack on Bahrain in three days and new tanker strikes in Hormuz. Easing: down from $95.84 on Friday.

Why it matters: Cheaper crude directly lowers India's import bill and fuel costs and should start to cool the fuel-led rise in wholesale inflation.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook +2, Fiscal & trade balance +1, Rupee +1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: Fourth tanker hit in Hormuz in 24 hours; Indian Navy deploys ships to escort vessels
item.description:
The UK maritime agency confirmed projectile strikes that disabled tankers; Iran claims six have sunk since Sunday, unverified. The US said its navy could escort ships with a coalition, and a third US carrier arrived. Escalating.

Why it matters: Attacks raise war-risk premiums and crew danger on India's main crude and LNG route, though naval escorts and recovering flows limit supply loss.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −1, Inflation outlook −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Houthis seize the Bab el-Mandeb gateway as Saudi-backed forces retreat; more ships divert
item.description:
The capture tightens Houthi control of the Red Sea entrance even as a container alliance resumes Suez services and plans more transits. Reverses part of last week's easing.

Why it matters: Renewed Red Sea risk threatens the freight-cost relief Indian exporters to Europe were beginning to see from carriers returning to Suez.

Market gauges: Growth outlook −1, Inflation outlook −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Nasdaq falls 2.49% and S&P 500 1.92% as new US AI-chip export curbs deepen the tech sell-off
item.description:
The rule limits chip sales to overseas data centres serving restricted countries; reports say India is not among markets facing the new licensing step. The US 10-year yield eased to about 5.12%. Escalating from Friday.

Why it matters: A US tech rout can weigh on Indian IT stocks and client spending, but money leaving AI trades has been flowing to India, and exemption helps local data-centre plans.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows +1, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) −1

Confidence: low · horizon: weeks

item.title: Wheat cargo ship sinks off Bulgaria after a suspected drone strike; European wheat futures climb
item.description:
All 12 crew were rescued. Türkiye is holding talks with Russia and Ukraine on resuming grain shipments. Separately, India's edible oil import bill rose 24% to a record ₹2 trillion in 2025-26. Escalating.

Why it matters: Black Sea disruption raises world wheat and sunflower-oil prices and freight, adding to India's food import costs while rabi sowing lags.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −1, Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks
